author: DebConf 25
title: Reviving (un)schroot?
content:
by Helmut Grohne


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/170-reviving-unschroot/


The schroot tool has been the primary build backend used by sbuild for a long time. More and more work has gone into a new unshare backend that we are slowly transitioning to. It solves several problems with schroot ranging from convenience, via security to reproducibility. However, the unshare backend comes with several downsides. Effectively, it bundles a container runtime into sbuild. The new backend inevitably regresses some use cases such as conveniently interacting with chroot environments outside builds. The question arises: Can we provide the improvements gained from unshare via the schroot API to sbuild? I will present a proof-of-concept, its limitations and request feedback regarding what features are needed to make it practically useful.


Room: Grand amphi


Scheduled start: 2025-07-15 11:30:00+02:00

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Activists Face ‘Terror’ Charges for ‘Vandalising Trump’s Golf Course’
content:
Prosecutors are seeking to

establish a “terrorism connection”

 in the case of seven Palestine Action activists who allegedly spray-painted Donald Trump’s golf course in Scotland.


The seven have been charged with malicious damage over the 8 March 2025 protest, which came weeks after Trump proposed a US-led takeover of the Gaza strip, the Guardian reported. 


Activists broke into the US president’s Turnberry golf course and spray-painted the message “Gaza is not 4 sale” on the lawn. They also sprayed weed killer and daubed the clubhouse in red paint. 


“The prosecution will seek to establish a ‘terror connection’, to enable terror sentences to be imposed on the defendants even though the prosecution has chosen not to charge them with any terror offences,” said campaign group Defend Our Juries (DOJ).


Trump had two phone calls with then prime minister Keir Starmer after the protest, DOJ added. 


The president referred to the protesters as “terrorists” in a post on Truth Social at the time of the incident – but a report by the Scottish terrorism board published in May 2025 concluded that the protest “has not been close to meeting the statutory definition of terrorism”. 


Some have questioned whether Trump influenced the decision to later designate Palestine Action as a terrorist group in the UK in July 2025.


On Wednesday, Trump’s own administration designated Palestine Action a terror group and announced it would sanction any members based in the US. 


A spokesperson for DOJ said: “It’s now all too clear why the White House has designated Palestine Action as a global terror organisation, alongside Al Qaeda. It’s because members of Palestine Action upset the president in March 2025 by making a mess of his golf course.”


Labour MP John McDonnell said: “The government has serious questions to answer about the allegations that Donald Trump politically interfered in this matter.”


“It would be utterly shameful if the British government launched an unprecedented attack on free speech in our country – resulting in more than 3,500 people being arrested under terrorism laws for peacefully holding seven-word signs – because Donald Trump threw a tantrum over some red paint on his golf course,” he added. 


Autumn Taylor Ward, Dylan Chiaramello, Ricky Southall, Kieran Robson, Rebecca Sian Davies, Uzma Bashir and John Moxley will have their first hearing at the High Court in Glasgow on Monday 31 August.

author: Ellen Cassedy
title: Dolly Parton Helped Us to Speak Up and Join Together
content:
Dolly Parton’s song, “9 to 5,” has endured as a beloved anthem for nearly half a century.  What many people don’t know is that the direct inspiration for the song—and the hit movie—was the 9 to 5 working women’s movement that began in Boston in the early 1970’s.  It was the movement that inspired the song and the movie—and the song and the movie gave the movement a giant boost.


In 1972, I was one of ten women office workers who started sitting in a circle on our lunch hour talking about our jobs.  We talked about low pay.  Unequal pay.  Training men to be our own supervisors.  Having to do favors—all kinds of favors— for our bosses.


Before long, our group became a significant factor in Boston’s labor scene.  Wielding media coverage, government pressure, and creative demonstrations of office workers’ discontent, we won millions of dollars in back pay and raises and improved women’s job situation throughout the city.  After a few years we went national, with chapters from coast to coast, and our woman-led union, District 925 of the Service Employees (SEIU), began to take shape.


Enter Jane Fonda.  Jane knew one of our leaders, Karen Nussbaum, from the antiwar movement, and when she said she’d decided to make a movie about the concerns of office workers, we were over the moon.  She met with our members to plumb their frustrations, revenge fantasies, and aspirations.  And in a stroke of genius, she invited Dolly to join the cast.


Dolly was already a superstar as a singer and songwriter, but she’d never been in a film.  Alongside Jane and comedian Lily Tomlin, she turned out to be a natural in her role as Doralee Rhodes, the sweet and greatly annoyed target of lecherous attention from her evil boss.


One day on the set she took out her guitar.  “I’ve got a song,” she said.


Her toe-tapping tune perfectly encapsulated working women’s grievances and our dreams.  It begins with pride, moves on to anger, then summons a sense of collective purpose.  It ends with victory: “The tide’s gonna turn, and it’s all gonna roll your way!”


Before 9 to 5, office workers had never been the main characters on the big screen.  In fact, although we were 20 million strong—one third of America’s female workforce—we were basically invisible.  When people pictured a worker, they saw a man in a hard hat brandishing a wrench.  But now audiences were laughing and cheering as the three women managed to remove their boss from the office and implement a slew of worker-friendly policies, from job-sharing to flex-time to child care.


The film made clear that the problem was the boss, not the secretaries, and that the answer was women taking collective action.  As people howled at the boss’s ridiculous antics, they realized that the old ways had to go.  The American office was never the same.


One morning shortly after the movie came out when I was riding the bus to work, I overheard one woman talking to another. “So I said to him,” she said, “‘No, I will not make your coffee!’ I just saw 9 to 5!”


Dolly’s way of contributing to that sea-change was all her own.


While Jane Fonda headlined our public events and spoke eloquently to the media about our issues, Dolly did not.  She walked no picket lines and made no public statements. Instead, she served as a powerful model.  She knew working women, knew the obstacles to success from the inside.  Her warmth and empathy were boundless.  Just by being who she was, she helped forge a path for countless women, helping them to move forward from silence to making common cause with coworkers.


In 2019, the podcaster Jad Abumrad asked Dolly if she thought of herself as a feminist.  “No, I do not,” she responded.  “I think of myself as a woman in business.”


Later she spoke a bit differently to

Time

 magazine.  "I suppose I am a feminist,” she said, “if I believe that women should be able to do anything they want to."


Such statements were typical of many of the women who joined 9 to 5.  They didn’t see themselves as part of the women’s liberation movement, yet they believed passionately in fairness and equality on the job.  Our movement worked hard to provide a safe space for such women, along with those who did feel comfortable with the feminist label.  Dolly’s example and her outsized presence helped us create that safe space and build unity among women all along the political spectrum.


Decade after decade, Dolly helped us to speak up and join together.  We owe her a debt.

author: David Swanson
title: End Global Militarization. CLOSE ALL BASES. U.S. Troops Out of Asia NOW!
content:
By Jhay de Jesus, Asia Organizer, World BEYOND War, August 28, 2026


In many places, U.S. military bases pose significant threats and risks to local communities and sectors. Regular base operations and military exercises have led to environmental destruction, the displacement of Indigenous communities from their ancestral lands, and an increase in human rights violations, particularly gender-based violence.


It must end now!


U.S. military installations

 account for 70% to 85% of all foreign military bases worldwide, spanning over 800 bases across 95 countries and territories.


In our

latest report

, World BEYOND War found that Europe hosts the highest proportion of U.S. bases at 38%, followed by East Asia and the Pacific at 28.2%.


U.S. Bases and Agreements in East and Southeast Asia


A quick search shows that U.S. military bases and other facilities currently total 245 sites in the region, including those classified as major bases, unclassified permanent installations, or smaller facilities such as communication outposts and shared host-nation sites.


Japan hosts the largest number of U.S. bases in Asia and ranks second globally, with more than 100 sites and 55,000 personnel. South Korea ranks second in Asia and third globally, with over 70 bases and 29,000 personnel. The Philippines is third in the region, with a total of 13 military sites. Other countries hosting smaller U.S. military presences include Thailand, Singapore, Cambodia, and Taiwan.


These bases result from various bilateral military agreements that the U.S. maintains to secure its interests and protect its regional hegemony. Several key agreements remain in place, including the Military Assistance Agreement with Thailand (1950), the

Mutual Defense Treaty

 with the Philippines (1951), the

Mutual Defense Treaty

 with South Korea (1953), and the

Treaty

 of Mutual Cooperation and Security with Japan (1960). Furthermore, the

Taiwan Relations Act

 of 1979 serves as a U.S. domestic law requiring Washington to provide Taiwan with weapons.


Japan’s 100-plus U.S. military sites feature several major hubs, with a heavy concentration in Okinawa Prefecture. These primary hubs include Kadena Air Base (for Air Force power projection), Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, and U.S. Army Garrison Okinawa (Torii Station). Across Honshu, facilities include Yokota Air Base—home to United States Forces Japan (USFJ) and the Fifth Air Force—Yokosuka Naval Base (home port of the U.S. 7th Fleet), Camp Zama (U.S. Army Japan), and Misawa Air Base in Aomori Prefecture. Additionally, Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni and Sasebo Naval Base are located in Yamaguchi and Nagasaki Prefectures, respectively. These bases are positioned to provide rapid-response capabilities across the Western Pacific, the Taiwan Strait, and the South China Sea.


In the Philippines, the Mutual Defense Treaty paved the way for subsequent agreements that allowed the U.S. to expand its military footprint. The

Visiting Forces Agreement

 (VFA) governs the entry, status, and criminal jurisdiction regarding U.S. military personnel staying temporarily in the country. This agreement was ratified solely by the Philippine Senate, without reciprocal legislative approval in the U.S. The

Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement

 (EDCA) serves as an operational and logistical framework allowing U.S. troops to rotate through designated “agreed locations,” preposition supplies, and construct joint-use infrastructure. These agreements have increased troop rotations and led to instances of crimes committed by U.S. personnel with limited accountability under Philippine law. High-profile cases, such as the Subic rape case and the murder of transgender woman Jennifer Laude, resulted in the perpetrators being transferred back to U.S. custody rather than serving their sentences in a local Philippine jail.


In South Korea, the Mutual Defense Treaty led to the creation of the Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) and the

Special Measures Agreement

 (SMA). In 2024, both nations signed the 12th SMA, covering the 2026–2030 period. Under this agreement, South Korea helps fund the cost of stationing U.S. Forces Korea. The agreement supports the joint defense posture and the presence of roughly 28,500 U.S. troops by covering non-personnel operational expenses outside the standard SOFA framework. South Korea’s contribution for 2026 is set at 1.52 trillion won (approximately $1.13 billion), an 8.3% increase from 2025 …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "The Lion King" in Quechua?: New Film "Runa Simi" Profiles Indigenous Artist Keeping Language Alive
content:
Experts estimate that a language is lost every two weeks — and that half of the world’s 7,000 spoken languages could be lost by the end of the century. Quechua is the most widely spoken Indigenous language in the Americas, with approximately 7 to 10 million speakers living primarily in Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador. But like so many Indigenous languages, Qechua is vulnerable due to cultural pressures and discrimination.


The new documentary

Runa Simi

 — “our language” in Quechua — follows Fernando Valencia, a Peruvian voice actor, Indigenous activist, radio host and single father, who has dubbed many online clips of animated movies into Quechua from his home in Cusco, Peru. In the film, Fernando pursues his most ambitious goal yet: to fully dub Disney’s animated classic

The Lion King

 into Quechua, with the help of his 8-year-old son, Dylan.


“I am sharing our culture to the worldwide culture,” says Fernando Valencia, who started dubbing films after noticing that Quechua-speaking Indigenous children were watching movies dubbed into Spanish that they couldn’t understand.


“There’s like one hour a week of Quechua [in school], so it is very hard to actually learn it,” says Fernando’s son Dylan, who is now 14 years old.


“Indigenous people in Peru are fighting for basic rights, like having water, electricity, healthcare, education in their own language,” says Augusto Zegarra, the director of

Runa Simi

. “But they also have the right to access entertainment in their own language.”

title: The Proletariat and the Possibility of Revolution - Agustín Guillamón
content:
The difference between Miquel Amorós and myself doesn’t lie in one wanting revolution and the other rejecting it, nor in one defending autonomy and the other not. [...] [W]hen we try to define what this autonomy means, what relationship it should have with the transformation of society, and, above all, who can carry this transformation to its ultimate consequences, a fundamental difference emerges between us.

I would say that this difference can be formulated as follows: Amorós emphasises the concrete reconstruction of autonomous forms of life, while I consider it necessary to ask about the social subject capable of transforming these necessarily partial experiences into a general transformation of capitalist relations. This is not about denying the value of autonomous experiences, nor about postponing emancipation to an indefinite future. It is about determining what social force can transform what today appears as a limited experience into a general way of organising life. This question necessarily leads to the proletariat, and in it, in my view, lies the essential difference between our respective positions.

Translated from Spanish at Kaosenlared, Publicado el 27 de agosto de 2026 / Por Agustín Guillamón.

The difference between Miquel Amorós and myself doesn’t lie in one wanting revolution and the other rejecting it, nor in one defending autonomy and the other not. We both start from a radical critique of capitalist society and the conviction that emancipation cannot be the work of institutions separate from those who struggle. We both reject the integration of struggles into state institutions and deeply distrust any organisation that seeks to replace direct worker action. However, when we try to define what this autonomy means, what relationship it should have with the transformation of society, and, above all, who can carry this transformation to its ultimate consequences, a fundamental difference emerges between us.

I would say that this difference can be formulated as follows: Amorós emphasises the concrete reconstruction of autonomous forms of life, while I consider it necessary to ask about the social subject capable of transforming these necessarily partial experiences into a general transformation of capitalist relations. This is not about denying the value of autonomous experiences, nor about postponing emancipation to an indefinite future. It is about determining what social force can transform what today appears as a limited experience into a general way of organising life. This question necessarily leads to the proletariat, and in it, in my view, lies the essential difference between our respective positions.

Amorós begins with a historical observation that cannot be ignored. The traditional forms of the workers’ movement have been profoundly weakened by the evolution of capitalism. Political representation, union integration, the fragmentation of labour, and the transformation of lifestyles have destroyed a good part of the conditions that allowed the proletariat to constitute itself, at certain historical moments, as a visible, organised revolutionary force capable of directly intervening in society. Faced with this situation, passively awaiting a future revolutionary recomposition would be a form of impotence. If emancipation has any real content, it must begin in the present.

Hence the importance that autonomy, community, and concrete utopia acquire in Amorós’s work. Revolution cannot be a promise that indefinitely justifies the acceptance of a subjugated life. We must reclaim now the capacities that capitalism has taken from us: To decide collectively, to produce and reproduce life without delegating it, to rebuild community ties, to recover knowledge, and to create spaces where human relations are not entirely determined by commodities and the state. This “concrete utopia” precisely expresses the desire not to postpone freedom until an uncertain future.

This demand strikes me as profoundly revolutionary. A revolution that doesn’t transform life would be a purely political revolution and, therefore, insufficient. We don’t want to change those who govern only to continue living under social relations we don’t control. We want the production, reproduction, and organisation of our existence to cease appearing to us as external powers. Emancipation cannot be reduced to modifying the administration of a society that remains essentially the same.

title: Shut Down The Stowe School Beagles!
content:
Today the Hunt Saboteurs Association can exclusively reveal the full footage that led to the recent conviction of Stowe School Beagles Kennel Huntsman Philip Kennedy for killing a hare in November 2025.


This is the first step in our campaign to shut down this hunt.


The footage shows both the extent of the cruelty of the Stowe School Beagles and the catastrophic failure of safeguarding at the £47,000 per year school.


Unbelievably, Kennedy is employed as a ‘Games Coach’ at Stowe and the hare hunting shown in the video is essentially a PE lesson, just like the rugby and hockey that is also offered at the school.


The Stowe School Beagles pursue the hare across a car park.


As the video opens, unsupervised Stowe pupils are looking for hares in the open Northamptonshire countryside. On their return to Crockwell Farm, the hounds are put into a strip of woodland by the farm’s car park. The hunters are there for some time – they obviously know a hare is present – before the hounds flush the terrified animal out across the car park.


Huntsman pats hounds as they rip into the hare.


The pursuit continues through a larger wood, with Kennedy positioning himself on its far side in case the hare breaks cover. The video next picks up the last moments of the doomed animal: she sprints across open ground – closely pursued by the whole pack – before crashing into a fence. She is obviously gravely injured but limps on before being overwhelmed by the pack.


Handshakes all round as the hare is ragged by the hounds.


The hunters arrive on the scene, patting the hounds and exchanging congratulatory handshakes as the hare is ripped to pieces. Back at the hound van and Stowe School minibus, the celebrations continue.


With the hare hunting season about to begin we cannot allow this cruelty to continue: the HSA will shortly be asking you – our valued supporters – to take action.

Please keep an eye on our socials over the next few days.

title: Gino ne doit pas être extradé !
content:
Le 19/08 la Cour d'Appel de Paris s'est récemment prononcé en faveur de l'extradition de notre camarade Gino vers l'Allemagne qui pourrait à son tour l'extrader vers la Hongrie.


Comme de nombreux·ses autres camarades Gino est pourchassé par la Hongrie pour sa participation à une action antifasciste contre le «

 

Jour de l'Honneur

 

», un rassemblement annuel de néo-nazis à Budapest.


Après avoir été une première fois arrêté en France et menacé d'extradition vers la Hongrie, Gino risque aujourd'hui l'extradition vers l'Allemagne où il encourt 10 ans de prison et une extradition vers la Hongrie. author: PETA-Team
title: Erfolg: Emma Matratzen beendet Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall
content:
Seit 2022 finanziert die Hong Kong Technology Venture Company Limited (HKTV) dutzende tödliche

Tierversuche

: Dabei werden Schweinen und Schafen in Experimenten Gliedmaßen und ihre Köpfe abgetrennt. Das Unternehmen ist die Muttergesellschaft von HKTVmall, einer der bekanntesten Online-Shopping-Plattformen Hongkongs.


Mit den Experimenten soll Technologie entwickelt werden, um Organe von Tieren für eine mögliche

Transplantation in Menschen

 zu nutzen. Dabei räumt HKTV selbst ein, dass die Versuche in hohem Maße spekulativ seien und es „keine Garantie“ für einen künftigen Nutzen für Menschen gebe.[1]


PETA USA und PETA Asien machen seit Frühjahr 2026 mit Protesten, Gesprächen mit Geschäftspartnern und weiteren Aktionen Druck auf HKTV. Die Kampagne zeigt Wirkung: Mehrere Unternehmen haben ihre Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall beendet oder angekündigt, dies zu tun. Im August 2026 kam mit dem deutschen, international agierenden Matratzenhersteller Emma ein weiteres großes Unternehmen hinzu.


Erfolg nach PETA-Gesprächen: Emma beendet Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall


Im August 2026 gab der Matratzenhersteller Emma bekannt, seinen Onlineshop auf HKTVmall bis Ende des Jahres zu schließen und die Geschäftsbeziehung vollständig zu beenden. Zuvor hatte PETA das Unternehmen darüber informiert, dass die Muttergesellschaft von HKTVmall tödliche Experimente an Schweinen und Schafen finanziert. 


Damit reiht sich Emma in eine wachsende Zahl von Unternehmen ein, die nach Bekanntwerden der Tierversuche Konsequenzen gezogen haben. Nach Beendigung der Geschäftsbeziehung sollen auch keine Provisionen oder Gebühren von Emma mehr an die Shopping-Plattform fließen. 


Die Emma

 Matratzen GmbH

 erklärte zu der Entscheidung: 


„Bei Emma wissen wir, dass guter Schlaf auch bedeutet, ein reines Gewissen zu haben. Sobald wir von den besorgniserregenden Tierversuchen erfahren haben, die von der Muttergesellschaft von HKTVmall finanziert werden, haben wir entschieden, unsere Geschäftsbeziehung mit HKTVmall nicht fortzusetzen. Der Shop wird geschlossen und die Geschäftsbeziehung bis Ende des Jahres vollständig beendet. Wir schätzen und unterstützen es, dass PETA uns darauf aufmerksam gemacht hat.“ 

Emma Matratzen GmbH

 


Weitere Unternehmen beenden Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall


Emma ist nicht das erste Unternehmen, das die Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall wegen der Tierversuche beendet. Bereits im Frühjahr 2026 hatten mindestens drei weitere Unternehmen öffentlich Konsequenzen gezogen: 


das Kosmetikunternehmen Lush Asia Limited, 


das Unternehmen für Gesundheitsprodukte für tierische Mitbewohner Pawfect Reborn, 


der Essenslieferdienst Fitasty. 


Lush Asia Limited begründete seinen Rückzug ausdrücklich mit Bedenken wegen der Tierversuche innerhalb der Unternehmensgruppe. Das Unternehmen erklärte, auch eine indirekte finanzielle Unterstützung solcher Experimente vermeiden zu wollen. 


Die Reaktionen zeigen: Öffentlicher Druck und die direkte Ansprache von Geschäftspartnern können konkrete Veränderungen bewirken.


Was passiert bei den von HKTV finanzierten Tierversuchen? 


Nach Informationen von PETA USA und PETA Asien finanziert HKTV seit 2022 dutzende Experimente, bei denen Schweine und Schafe verstümmelt und getötet werden. Dabei werden den Tieren unter anderem ihre Gliedmaßen und Köpfe abgetrennt.


Mit den Versuchen sollen Technologien für Organtransplantationen entwickelt werden. Organe von Tieren sollen dabei auf ihre Eignung für eine mögliche Transplantation in Menschen untersucht werden.


Wir von PETA Deutschland und unsere internationalen Partnerorganisationen kritisieren diese Experimente nicht nur aus

ethischen Gründen

. Es stehen auch

tierversuchsfreie Methoden

 zur Verfügung, um menschliche Gesundheit, Organerhaltung, Geweberegeneration und Transplantationsverfahren zu untersuchen.


PETA USA und PETA Asien fordern das Unternehmen daher auf, die Finanzierung der Tierversuche unverzüglich zu beenden und auf tierfreie Methoden umzusteigen.


April 2026: Proteste und erste Unternehmen wenden sich von HKTVmall ab 


Im April 2026 wandte sich PETA Asien schriftlich an die Unternehmensleitung und forderte ein sofortiges Ende der Experimente. 


Auch vor der Zentrale von HKTVmall machten Aktive auf das Leid der Tiere aufmerksam. Bei einer Protestaktion trugen sie blutverschmierte Overalls sowie übergroße Schweine- und Schafsmasken. Mit symbolischen Tierköpfen, einer riesigen Spritze und einem blutverschmierten Messer …

title: “Sınırda Çocuk Var” diyerek Kapıköy’den Kilis’e yürüyecek
content:
Davranış analisti ve çocuk gelişim uzmanı Tanyel Süzer, çocukların yaşam hakkına dikkat çekmek için Türkiye-İran sınırındaki Kapıköy’den başlayıp Kilis’e kadar uzanacak bir yürüyüşe hazırlanıyor. “Yaşam Hakkı Yürüyüşü” adını verdiği projeyle bölge illerinden geçecek olan Süzer, çocukların savaş, yoksulluk, şiddet, istismar ve eşitsizlik nedeniyle karşı karşıya kaldıkları hak ihlallerini gündeme taşımayı hedefliyor.


Süzer yürümeye Kapıköy’den başlayacak.


Van, Hakkari, Şırnak, Mardin, Urfa ve Antep üzerinden ilerleyerek Kilis sınır kapısında yürüyüşünü tamamlamayı planlıyor.


Yol boyunca her hafta çocuk haklarının farklı bir alanını gündeme getirecek; geçtiği illerde sivil toplum örgütleriyle bir araya gelmeye, yerelde yaşanan hak ihlallerini dinlemeye ve çocukların haklarına ilişkin çözüm önerilerini görünür kılmaya çalışacak.


Bu yolculuğun temasını ise üç kelimeyle anlatıyor:


“Sınırda Çocuk Var.”


Süzer, rotasını belirlerken sınır illerini bilinçli olarak seçtiğini söylüyor. Rota üzerindeki illerde çocuk nüfusunun yüksekliğine ve kırsalda yaşayan çocukların toplumsal yaşama erişiminde karşılaştıkları güçlüklere dikkat çekiyor:


"Bir taraftan çocuk nüfusu açısından çok kalabalık illerden oluşurken bir taraftan da kırsal bölgelerde çocukların toplumsal yaşama erişimi çok kısıtlı ve bir süre sonra çocuksuz, gençsiz kalan köyler var."


Komşu ülkelerde yaşanan savaşların beraberinde getirdiği göç ve yoksulluğun çocuklar üzerindeki etkilerinin de yürüyüşün çıkış noktalarından biri olduğunu anlatıyor.


Dünyanın neredeyse tamamında sınırların her iki tarafında da hem kalan hem giden çocukların yaşadıkları hak ihlallerine dikkat çekmek amacıyla bir farkındalık eylemi gerçekleştirmek istedim.


Kapıköy’den başlayan sembolik rota


Süzer için Kapıköy yalnızca yürüyüşün coğrafi başlangıç noktası değil.


İran’da yaşanan savaş sırasında bir okulun bombalanması ve kız çocuklarının yaşamını yitirmesine ilişkin haberlerin kendisini derinden etkilediğini söylüyor.


"Böyle katliamları unutmamam için İran-Türkiye sınır kapısı olan Kapıköy’den başlamanın anlamlı olacağını düşündüm."


Buradan başlayan yürüyüş boyunca Süzer yalnızca çocukların yaşadığı sorunları sıralamak istemiyor. Çocuk haklarının hangi yasal dayanaklarla güvence altında olduğunu ve hak ihlallerinin önlenmesi için neler yapılabileceğini de tartışmaya açmayı planlıyor.


Her hafta farklı çocuk hakları ve ihlal alanlarına yönelik temaları gündeme getirerek hem bölgede yaşanan hak ihlallerini görünür kılmak hem de yasal dayanakları ve hak ihlallerinin çözümüne ilişkin örnekleri ve görüşleri paylaşarak çocuk hakları temelinde politikalar geliştirilmesi için kamuoyu oluşturabilmeyi umuyorum.


“Bir şey yapmam lazım, eylemde olmaya ihtiyacım var”


Yaşam Hakkı Yürüyüşü fikrinin ardında Süzer’in uzun yıllara yayılan gönüllülük ve çocuklarla çalışma deneyiminin yanı sıra son yıllarda takip ettiği gelişmeler de var.


Lise yıllarında Babaeski Halkevi’nde bir izci kulübü kurarak başlayan gönüllülük hikâyesi, üniversite döneminde 1999 depremlerindeki arama kurtarma çalışmalarına destek vermesiyle devam etti. 2002’de okul öncesi öğretmenliği bölümünden mezun oldu. Özel eğitim ve rehabilitasyon merkezlerinde çalıştı; arama kurtarma alanında köpek eğitimi üzerine gönüllülük yaptı. Daha sonra Düşler Akademisi ve Kızlar Atakta gibi projelerde yer aldı.


Engelli hakları, kız çocuklarının güçlendirilmesi, toplumsal cinsiyet eşitliği ve çocuk hakları alanlarında çalışan Süzer, son üç yıldır ağırlığını çocuk haklarına verdiğini söylüyor.


Ancak yürüyüş kararını yalnızca mesleki geçmişiyle açıklamıyor.


Türkiye’de çocukların şiddet, istismar, yoksulluk ve ihmalle karşı karşıya kaldığını; barınma, eğitim, sağlık, beslenme, oyun, kültür ve sanat gibi temel haklarının ihlal edildiğini belirten Süzer, çocuk işçiliği, suça sürüklenme ve cinsel istismar vakalarının kendisinde giderek büyüyen bir harekete geçme ihtiyacı yarattığını söylüyor.


Sadece yazıp çizmek, bazen oturup ağlamak, bazen de sokaklara çıkıp öfkeyle haykırmak bana yetmiyor. Bir şey yapmam lazım, eylemde olmaya ihtiyacım var.


Tanyel Süzer ve Cüce


“Sadece kendi çocuklarımızı korumak gerçek çözüm değil”


Süzer’in yürüyüşle tartışmaya açmak istediği temel meselelerden biri de çocukların korunmasının kimin sorumluluğu olduğu.


Ona göre çocuk hakları yalnızca ebeveynlerin ya da çocuklarla çalışan kuruluşların meselesi değil.


"Eğer sadece kendi çocuklarımızın ya da en fazla yakın çevremizdeki çocukların …

title: Li Nepalê hejmara miriyan derket 469an
content:
Li ser sînorê Nepal û Tîbetê xebatên lêgerîn û rizgarkirinê yên ji bo kesên ku di lehiya 26ê Tebaxê de winda bûne didomin. Tîmên Nepalî û Çînî bi hev re mil bi mil dixebitin. Li gorî zanyariyên fermî yên dawî, hejmara miriyan gihîştiye 469 kesan.


667 kes winda ne


Emniyeta Nepalê têkildarî karesatê daxuyanî da û weha got:


“Di lehiya Bhotekoshiyê de hejmara miriyan gihîşt 469 kesan. Bi sedan kes jî winda ne. Tîmên lêgerînê li seranserê rûbar û deverên jêrîn ji bo dîtina kesên sax û cenazeyan xebatên xwe berdewam dikin. Di nav kesên winda de gelek geştiyar û çiyager jî hene. Desteya Geştiyariyê ya Nepalê şeva Pêncşemê di daxuyaniya xwe de ragihand ku li herêmên ku lehî rabûye, 127 jê Nepallî bi giştî 667 geştiyar û rêwî hêj winda ne.”


Cemed û zinar herifîn


Karesata lehiyê, li herêma Langtang Lirungê ya Hîmalayayan ji ber herifîna cemedekê ku ji herî, av û zinaran pêk dihat, çêbûye.


Li gorî nûçeya The Guardianê, pisporan diyar kir ku beşeke mezin a cemed, zinar û heriyê ber bi geliyan ve herikîne û di  Çemê Trishuliyê ya Nepalê û deverên niştecihbûnê yên Tîbetê de bûne sedema lehiyên gelek wêranker.

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 28 août
content:
Le 28 août, c'est dans la rue que l'éphéméride des luttes se trouve. Elle est dans toutes les grèves, toutes les émeutes et tous les braquages que ce jour a pu voir surgir à travers les années.


1886 :

 A Lyon, parution du premier numéro de la 'Lutte Sociale'.


1926 :

 Au Nicaragua, les Marines US débarquent pour protéger les intérêts des États-Unis contre la révolte sandiniste, qui avait réalisé une collectivisation des terres et luttait contre l'instauration d'un capitalisme de monopole.


1927 :

 A Charleston aux Etats-Unis, ce sont les funérailles des anarchistes italiens Sacco et Vanzetti, exécutés à la chaise électrique quelques jours plus tôt. Des milliers de personnes y assistent.


1936 :

 En Espagne, au cours de la guerre civile, "

près de Huesca en Aragon (Espagne), la section italienne de la Colonne Ascaso guidée par le républicain Mario Angeloni, l'antifasciste libertaire Carlo Rosselli, Camillo Berneri et Umberto Tommasini, repousse une attaque des franquistes. Mais Mario Angeloni et les anarchistes Michele Centrone, Fosco Falaschi et Vincenzo Perrone trouvent la mort lors de ces combats.

"


Repris de l'éphéméride anarchiste


1943 :

 Au Danemark, grève générale dans tout le pays contre l'occupant nazi.


1944 :

 Libération de Marseille et de Toulon par les Alliés.


1954 :

 Mort du cambrioleur anarchiste Alexandre Marius Jacob, né en 1879 à Marseille.


1963 :

 Aux Etats-Unis, Martin Luther King Jr. prononce son célèbre discours '

I Have a Dream

'.


1964 :

 - A Philadelphie aux USA, une émeute se déclenche et durera trois jours après une énième démonstration de violences policières contre la communauté noire de la ville. 225 magasins sont détruits.


 Le même jour, Bob Dylan fait gouter de la marijuana aux Beatles pour la première fois de leur vie.


1968 :

 A Chicago, une manifestation organisée par le comité contre la guerre du Vietnam en marge de la contestation du Congrès des Démocrates organisé à ce moment-là débouche sur des émeutes en ville. Mais il y avait 10.000 manifestant-e-s et 23.000 policiers.


1975 :

 A Londres, l'IRA fait exploser une voiture dans Oxford Street, sans que personne ne soit blessé.


1979 :

 A Bruxelles, l'IRA fait sauter une bombe sur la Grand Place.


1980 :

 - Dans le XVième arrondissement de Paris, fusillade entre des militants d'Action Directe et la police au cours d'un braquage de banque.


 A Condé-sur-L'Escaut, dans le Nord, un braquage de banque des autonomes rapporte 16 millions de francs.


1984 :

 A Paris, Action Directe réalise un attentat à l'explosif contre le siège du Parti Socialiste et contre le Ministère de la Défense.

 du 28 août.

title: 3ήμερο δράσεων για τα 3 χρόνια από την κρατική δολοφονία του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη, 28-30/8
content:
ΓΙΑ ΤΩΡΑ, ΓΙΑ ΠΑΝΤΑ ΚΑΙ ΓΙΑ ΟΣΟ ΧΡΕΙΑΣΤΕΙ ΑΥΤΕΣ ΟΙ ΜΕΡΕΣ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΟΥ ΚΩΣΤΗ


>ΠΑΡΑΣΚΕΥΗ 28 ΑΥΓΟΥΣΤΟΥ


19:00, αυλή του κατειλημμένου λόφου Καστέλι


Εκδήλωση-συζήτηση: «Ο δικαστικός εμπαιγμός ως μέρος της συγκάλυψης της αστυνομικής βίας»


Ενημέρωση από τις υποθέσεις κρατικών δολοφονιών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου, του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν και του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη.


Στη συζήτηση θα συμμετέχουν ο Γιάννης Μάγγος, πατέρας του Βασίλειου, ο Αναστάσης Μανιουδάκης, γιος του Κωστή, ο Θανάσης Καμπαγιάννης, δικηγόρος στην υπόθεση δολοφονίας του Κωστή, καθώς και μέλος της ανοιχτής συνέλευσης ενάντια στην κρατική δολοφονία του Μοχαμεντ Καμράν.


Η εισήγηση της ανοιχτής συνέλευσης για την κρατική δολοφονία του Κ. Μανιουδάκη:


Εισήγηση της εκδήλωσης «Ο δικαστικός εμπαιγμός ως μέρος της συγκάλυψης της αστυνομικής βίας» | 3 χρόνια από την κρατική δολοφονία του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη, Παρασκευή 28/08


>ΣΑΒΒΑΤΟ 29 ΑΥΓΟΥΣΤΟΥ


20:00, πλατεία δημοτικής Αγοράς


ΠΟΡΕΙΑ για τα τρία χρόνια από την κρατική δολοφονία του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη


>ΚΥΡΙΑΚΗ 30 ΑΥΓΟΥΣΤΟΥ


12:00, επαρχιακός δρόμος Φρε-Βρυσών στην έξοδο προς τον ΒΟΑΚ, στο ύψος των Βρυσών


Συγκέντρωση μνήμης στο σημείο της δολοφονίας του Κωστή


Στο σημείο αυτό, η ανοιχτή συνέλευση και αλληλέγγυα άτομα έχουμε τοποθετήσει από τον Φεβρουάριο του 2024, επιγραφή που αναφέρει «Σε αυτήν την περιοχή, το απόγευμα της 1ης Σεπτεμβρίου του 2023, αστυνομικοί των Τ.Α.Ε. δολοφόνησαν σε “τυχαίο έλεγχο” τον Κωστή Μανιουδάκη. Ο αγώνας ενάντια στην αστυνομική ασυδοσία και την κρατική βαρβαρότητα είναι αγώνας για την αξιοπρέπεια. title: Francia, antisemitismo e islamofobia: intervista a un attivista di UFJP
content:
Abbiamo intervistato un attivista de l’UJFP (Union Juive Française Pour La Paix) in merito ad alcuni temi all’ordine del giorno: l’antirazzismo e l’islamofobia, l’antisemitismo e l’antisionismo, per approfondire cosa si muove in Francia sul piano delle mobilitazioni e degli avanzamenti della soggettività organizzata su questo dibattito. E’ interessante la critica che il compagno ebreo decoloniale per la Palestina rivolge alla sinistra – istituzionale e non – individuando nella rigidità ideologica uno dei limiti nell’andare nella direzione di un movimento di massa contro la guerra e l’imperialismo.


Daniel è un attivista sindacale e insegnante di liceo nei quartieri popolari nella periferia di Parigi. In quanto ebreo, è anche attivista dell’Union Juive Française Pour La Paix (UJFP). Da tempo si occupa della questione palestinese e della lotta contro il sionismo nell’ambito delle attività sindacali e dei movimenti sociali. In questa intervista analizza il fenomeno dell’imperialismo e del riarmo europeo che si sta delineando sempre più chiaramente sia in Europa che al di fuori di essa. L’intervista è stata svolta a giugno 2026.


Buona lettura!


Mi chiamo Daniel, sono insegnante in periferia di Parigi. Faccio parte dell’Union Juive Française Pour la Paix, che lotta contro il razzismo e contro il colonialismo, per i diritti dei Palestinesi e sono sindacalista nel mio istituto scolastico e con gli insegnanti e il personale della scuola ho partecipato ai movimenti degli ultimi anni come i Gilet Gialli o Bloquons Tout ma anche agli scioperi dei lavoratori.


Come si possono interpretare i legami che diventano sempre più evidenti tra il sionismo e i discorsi politici di destra in Europa, il razzismo, l’islamofobia e l’imperialismo? Oggi c’è stata una rottura con il 7 ottobre e soprattutto dal genocidio massiccio dei Palestinesi ma diciamo che questo si inserisce in una continuità.


Prima di tutto, l’Europa ha sostenuto la creazione di Israele e l’espulsione dei Palestinesi fin dall’inizio, presentando ciò come un processo di autodeterminazione nazionale. Quindi c’è stato un rovesciamento dei valori e si è data la solidarietà a un progetto coloniale.


Questo è stato un atteggiamento permanente da parte delle grandi potenze imperialiste, che si trattasse dell’Europa, della Gran Bretagna, della Francia, della Germania, degli Stati Uniti, dell’URSS. Questo, all’inizio. Poi c’è stato un momento in cui hanno preteso di chiedere agli israeliani di fare degli accordi. Accordi che sono sempre stati ingiusti e sfavorevoli nei confronti dei Palestinesi oltre ad essere stato presentato come colpa dei Palestinesi da parte di Israele. Si parla di Nakba permanente, con una grande espulsione nel 1948, una grande espulsione nel 1967, e ora, molti morti da tre anni. Casa per casa, espulsione per espulsione, in modo permanente. Oggi vediamo un’accelerazione e un’ideologia che viene da Israele, che si presenta come la punta avanzata della civiltà occidentale in difesa di quella che viene considerata un’opposizione musulmana, che riproduce una guerra di civiltà, permeata di islamofobia, di autoritarismo e che trasgredisce tutte le norme di diritto comunemente accettate fino a questo momento.


Quindi ciò che vediamo in Israele risuona con ciò che accade in generale in Occidente, ossia il bisogno delle classi dominanti di entrare in una competizione esasperata che risponde a una sorta di crisi nell’accumulazione del profitto, il che aumenta lo sfruttamento. Per andare in questa direzione ci sono forse due vie, una via che conserva i diritti democratici e un’altra via, puramente di estrema destra fascista, che vuole affrancarsi dalle norme, e che quindi è arrivata al potere con Haider, Orbán, Meloni, Trump — beh, non in Europa ma… Quindi questa estrema destra si ispira a Israele, ma in realtà tutte le borghesie si muovono nella stessa direzione e quindi considerano la solidarietà con lo Stato d’Israele come qualcosa di essenziale. Quindi è vero che, vista questa radicalizzazione di Israele, ciò provoca una radicalizzazione delle classi dominanti occidentali.


Dunque, nel rapporto di dominazione e nella repressione altrettanto duratura rispetto alle colonie, nel rapporto coloniale con altri paesi o con le popolazioni provenienti dalle colonie che abitano le metropoli, c’è sempre stato un razzismo, una stigmatizzazione, un doppio standard nel trattamento. Ma ora, con la solidarietà alla Palestina, ci sono stati regolarmente tentativi di …

author: Unknown
title: «Ангелы в подвалах»: сборник о сирийской революции, написанный местными левыми
content:
Издательский кооператив «Напильник» совместно с исследовательским проектом «Hevale» продолжают распространять уникальную книгу о сирийской революции: «Ангелы в подвалах».

Сирийская революция началась как мирное народное восстание. У неё не было лидеров, партийных структур или внешней поддержки. Люди — молодежь, рабочие, женщины, интеллигенция — вышли на улицы, требуя свободы, достоинства, справедливости. Они создавали местные советы, формировали горизонтальные сети, отказывались от старых моделей власти.

Со страниц «Ангелов в подвалах» говорят те, кто прошёл через тюрьмы режима, осады и изгнание — и не сломался. Их опыт напоминает: будущее не гарантировано — но именно поэтому оно и остаётся возможным.

Стоимость – 1000 рублей, заказать можно через бот обратной связи телеграм-канала кооператива «Напильник».

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Giyotin İş Başında  —  II. BÖLÜM: Marksist Devletin Mutlakiyetçi ve Terörist Mahiyeti
content:
Yazan: Grigori Petroviç Maksimov


Çeviren: Scianus


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


Paris Komünü’nün demokrasisini savunurken Lenin, onun tam karşısını amaçlıyordu. Ve madem Lenin, kendi kuru ve akademik üslubuyla Marx ve Engels’in eserlerine son derece vâkıftır, o hâlde Karl Marx’ın Mart 1850’de Komünistler Birliği’ne yaptığı hitabede yer alan şu pasajdan haberdar olsa gerek:


“

Demokratlar ya federatif bir cumhuriyet için çaba göstereceklerdir ya da bölünmez bir cumhuriyet olmaksızın yapamayacaklarsa, hiç değilse komünlere ve vilâyetlere mümkün olan en geniş ölçüde özerklik ve inisiyatif tanıyarak merkezî hükümeti zayıflatmaya çalışacaklardır. Buna karşılık işçiler yalnızca tek ve bölünmez bir Alman cumhuriyeti için değil, iktidarın devletin ellerinde en güçlü biçimde merkezîleştirilmesi için de çaba göstermelidirler. Fransa’da 1793 yılında olduğu gibi, komünlerin özgürlüğü, özyönetim vb. hakkındaki bu demokratik gevezeliğin yemiyle kendilerini tuzağa düşürmemelidirler. Günümüz Almanya’sında mevcut iktidarın en güçlü biçimde merkezîleştirilmesini gerçekleştirmek, gerçekten devrimci bir partinin görevi hâline gelmelidir

.”

1


Lenin, “Devlet ve Devrim” adlı broşüründe Engels’in Bebel’e yazdığı mektuptan, şu sözlerle sona eren uzun bir pasaj aktarır:


“

Bizim

2

 devletimiz, mücadele sırasında, devrim içinde, muhaliflerimizi


zor yoluyla bastırmak amacıyla kullanılacak yalnızca geçici bir kurum olduğuna göre, özgür bir halk devletinden söz etmek düpedüz saçmalık olur; mevcut koşullar altında proletaryanın hâlâ Devlete ihtiyacı vardır; ancak buna özgürlük adına değil, düşmanlarını bastırabilmek için ihtiyaç duyar; özgürlük, ancak devletin kendisi varlığını sona erdirdiğinde gündemin konusu olacaktır

.”


Lenin, Rusya’daki “Sosyalist” inşanın örüntülerini işte bu zemin üzerine çizdi ve “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”nü bu temel üzerinde kurdu. Bunlar, Engels’in öğrettiği üzere, yalnızca proletaryanın düşmanlarına karşı değil, yalnızca kendi muhaliflerine karşı da değil, düşmanlarına karşı yürüttüğü mücadelenin yöntemlerinin hareket noktalarıydı. Lenin “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”nü şöyle tanımlar:


“

Proletaryanın devrimci Diktatörlüğü, proletaryanın ele geçirdiği ve burjuvazi üzerinde zor yoluyla sürdürdüğü iktidardır; bu, hiçbir yasayla bağlı olmayan bir iktidardır

.”

3


Lenin iktidarı ele geçirdiğinde, hiçbir yasayla kendisini bağlı saymaksızın bu “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”nü derhal uygulamaya koyuldu. Sol Sosyalist-Devrimcilerin gensorusuna verdiği cevap, ölüm cezasının kaldırılmasına duyduğu öfke ve Sosyalist bir koalisyon hükümeti kurma önerisini reddetmesi, bütün bunların kaynağı aynı yere götürülebilirdi: otokratik iktidar tutkusu; kibir ve ihtirastan doğan, dünyadaki ilk Marksist “İşçi Devleti”ni, kendi Bolşevik Devleti’ni, Engels’in ifadesiyle “Bizim Devletimiz”i kurma girişiminde bulunmaya yönelik yakıcı arzu; yani hakkında şöyle denebilecek bir Devlet:


“ … Devlet biziz, proletaryadır, işçi sınıfının öncü kesimidir.” “ … Devlet —bu, işçiler demektir, işçilerin ileri kesimi demektir; o, öncüdür, biziz.”

4


“Devlet biziz.” … Biz Parti’yiz ve Parti —yani parti ile parti aygıtı— benim. Öyleyse Devlet —benim ve yalnızca benim. Bir Marksist XIV. Louis—siyasal Marksizmin pratikte, yaşamın içinde mantıksal olarak açımlanmasının kaçınılmaz sonucu budur … İşçilerin Sosyalist Devleti, “Proletarya Diktatörlüğü”, bir XIV. Louis tarafından, yani iyiliksever bir despotizm, bir mutlakiyet tarafından taçlandırılmıştır. Bu, kaçınılmaz bir mantıksal zorunluluktur… “Bizim Devletimiz”, yalnızca düşmanlarımızı yok etmek için değil, esas olarak “muhaliflerimizi” bastırmak için kurulmuş mutlakiyetçi bir Devlettir. Ve muhaliflerin sayısı daima düşmanlardan fazladır. Düşmanlar kapitalistler, toprak sahipleri, generaller ve papazlardır. Muhaliflere gelince, bunlar her şeyden önce kolektif “biz”in sınırları dışında duran, yani Parti’nin dışında kalan kimseleri kapsar. “Bizim insanlarımız olmayan” milyonlarca insan, iki muhalif kategorisine ayrılır: kendi düşüncelerine sahip olan, kendi Sosyalist görüşlerini taşıyan ve Sosyalizmi kurmanın yol ve araçları hakkında kendi fikirleri bulunanlar. Çeşitli Sosyalist ve Anarşist gruplar, partiler, işçi sendikaları, kooperatifler, çeşitli dernekler — bütün bunlar doğrudan ve sürekli muhalifler sınıfına girer. Diğer grup ise, yalnızca zaman zaman, aralıklı olarak ve belirli vesilelerle kendi içlerinden muhalifler çıkaran geniş pasif kitlelerden, yani potansiyel muhalifler grubundan …

author: Bukola Oladunjoye
title: Living and Losing the ECOWAS Dream: Borders, Belonging, and Betrayal
content:
As I entered Benin, I waited for the air to change. I stood at that threshold with the quiet anticipation of someone expecting a revelation, for the people to look far apart from me, for some element of differentiation, something to confirm I was no longer in Nigeria. I was searching, almost desperately, for the feeling of foreignness. Instead, what greeted me was the mandatory walk on foot across a stretch of dusty no-man’s-land, the heat sitting on my shoulders like a familiar relative. There was the service charge for entry, slipped across a counter with the practiced nonchalance of a transaction that exists in no official ledger. And there were the sweaty hands that stamped my passport, unhurried, unbothered, as though the act of dividing one people from another was simply another Tuesday. Beyond that, not much. Only the invisible lines drawn by chubby hands across a colonial round table, lines that speak more to the boundaries of colonial reach than to any real difference in identity or people. The same okadas weaved through traffic on both sides. The same smell of fried plantain hung in the air. The same sun.


Benin


My first thought: why is there no train across this coast? A coast declared a unified body by ECOWAS long before Europe had anything resembling the Schengen region. A single rail line from Lagos to Accra, threading through Cotonou and Lomé, would do more for West African integration than a thousand protocols signed in air-conditioned conference rooms. The European Union did not become real to its people through treaties, it became real the moment a German student could board a train in Berlin and wake up in Paris without once showing a passport. We have the treaties. We have the protocols. We have been a free movement zone, on paper, since 1979. What we do not have is the infrastructure that turns a political agreement into a lived experience. Instead, we walk. We sweat. We pay.


My first real differentiation came through language. The local I approached spoke differently, but even that gap traced back to an interrupted history. His was a colonial tongue, French shaped by Beninese breath and rhythm, as much as the English I rushed to speak in return, hoping he would understand: ‘I’d like to book a ride to Ouidah.’ He looked at me with the patient amusement of someone who had translated themselves their entire life, and we found each other somewhere in the middle, two Africans borrowing the languages of our respective colonisers to speak to one another on African soil. There is something quietly absurd about that, and something quietly devastating. We were not foreign to each other. Only our inherited tongues were.


We stopped in Ouidah for a day and a half, and the city unfolded like a quiet invitation, an adventure of discovery that immediately planted the intention to return. There is a particular kind of place that refuses to be consumed in a single visit, that withholds just enough of itself to ensure you come back. Ouidah is that place. The best trips end on an unfinished note, like cutlery rested neatly across a plate, signalling: I am not done tasting this.


Ouidah


But Ouidah was painful to explore. Not the loud, declarative pain of a wound freshly opened, but the dull, persistent ache of something that has never properly healed. I could not stop my mind from wandering, what would this city’s reality look like without the colonial interruption? What identity would it have assumed, what architecture, what cuisine, what music, without the chaos of its exploitation? The Python Temple – a local devotional site hosting live snakes – still stands, its sacred serpents moving slowly across the cool floor, carrying in their bodies a spirituality that survived everything. The Zomachi market still hums. But underneath it all, Ouidah carries the weight of what was taken from it.


Standing at the Door of No Return, I felt the ground shift slightly beneath me, not physically, but in the way that certain places demand a recalibration of the self. The monument stands at the edge of the Atlantic, facing the ocean that swallowed so many. The same ocean that connects Lagos to the Americas, that carried away millions and brought back almost nothing. A line from a Christmas carol I had sung thoughtlessly for years suddenly split open with new meaning: for slave is our brother. I had sung it as a child in church, in the rote way of someone reciting words without weight. Standing there, the words gained …

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

here

.


Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.


US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.


Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.


Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.


Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.


Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.


In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.


Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment. 


On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro. 


Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.


Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.


RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.


Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.


And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations. 


Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.


The government plans to put its internal political dialogue on the New York agenda. The process, now being hurried in Khartoum, is to be presented as nationally owned, with international actors there to support and facilitate rather than dictate its agenda or outcome.


But a political source close to the dialogue said New York will test the international response to a process whose current, state-curated form is already being rejected by parts of the civilian political camp. 


Sudanese political and civilian forces, opposed to both the war and a military-led political process, rejected Burhan’s call for a dialogue, saying that any process launched while fighting continues — and conducted under military control — would reproduce …

author: Linda Ngari
title: Hybrid Repression: Coordinated Attacks on Rwanda Press Freedom
content:
The paradox of press freedom in Rwanda is that despite the advent of alternative media, younger journalists are more controlled than their older counterparts. “Today’s generation? Yeah, they’re getting more fear than we used to,” 47-year-old Rubens Mukunzi said in a phone interview. Rubens has experienced a Rwanda before Kagame’s 26-year presidency. He was 15 when the genocide that killed at least 800,000 Rwandans happened. The same year that 32-year-old Samuel Baker Byansi was born. While Rubens practised journalism in his home country for 13 years before he fled to America in 2013, Samuel practised for half the time, having started in 2016 and fleeing to Europe in 2022. Rubens had never been arrested for his work even though he earned the name “Mr Bean” from his comic commentary on Rwandan politics through his radio show at the time. But Samuel recalls being arrested more than four times for his work.


In a phone interview, Samuel narrates one of the arrests in 2022 that upended his plans to ask his girlfriend to marry him. “They arrested me for something not serious. I had tweeted that journalist

Kakwenza Rukirabashaija

 fled Uganda. I was detained for like four days. No communication. It disturbed me. I had my proposal that Saturday. I was arrested on Tuesday.” Samuel being arrested for a tweet is indicative of the government’s online surveillance to control free speech and limit the use of social media for political dissent.


Within three months of gathering this report, artist and YouTuber

Aimable Karasira

 was killed (May 6), and Rwandan authorities confirmed the arrest (May 1) of YouTubers Nsanzimana Augustin and Niyonshuti Emmanuel for “suspected spreading of false information” via their

YouTube channel

,

Imbarutso ya Demokarasi

 (The Rise of Democracy). Even though YouTubing is barely profitable in Rwanda since YouTube ads were

suspended

 in 2021. About 10 of the 13 imprisoned Rwandan journalists recorded on the Committee to Protect Journalists’

database

 are YouTubers, illustrating the paradox of press freedom in the country, where the rise of the internet and alternative media has ironically stirred up more repression.


As an early career journalist, Samuel underwent a compulsory civic education programme called

Itorero ry’Igihugu

. A report by Democracy in Africa explains that the programme was

introduced

 in 2009 as part of President Paul Kagame’s post-genocide ideology for the making of a “new Rwandan citizen”, known as

Umunyarwanda.

 Rubens, 30 at the time, was never a student of this programme. Samuel narrates his experience in his

book

 From

Watchdogs to Traitors: The less you know, the more you believe

. “The programme offers certificates symbolizing their support for the RPF. President Kagame holds the honorary title,

Intore Izirusha Intambwe

, a significant figure for all programme participants,” Samuel wrote. In the book, he recounts a time he was arrested for publishing a story titled “Eat and Die: Rwanda Supermarket Selling Toxic Meat”.


Samuel also mentions being offered US$500 by Rwandan authorities trying to recruit him as a government informant. “He [a police officer] expressed the desire to work closely with me in the interest of our country,” he wrote. The offer was backed by enticing dinners at high-end restaurants, free fuel at certain gas stations, tax exemptions, and a get-out-of-jail-free card for the times Samuel violated traffic rules.


 “In the beginning, of course, they don’t recruit you by telling you, ‘You are going to work for us,’ but they come as friends. ‘We want you to be friends with us. We have something to offer, which is a little bit better than what you earn.’  I remember when I bought my first car in Rwanda, and it was supposed to pay taxes of, like, five million Rwandan francs. And then one guy in the police intelligence called the revenue [Rwanda Revenue Authority] and told them, ‘Ah, this is our boy. You don’t need to tax him all this much.’ And just like that, I got my car without any tax paid. It’s like a psychological bribe somehow. So when the same person calls to ask for a favour of talking about someone online, you don’t have the capacity to say no. They give you all those privileges, and they give you this money, but in return you are compromising your own ethics, and this is what they want. But they also want you to maintain your credibility as a journalist, such that when you defend them, it becomes a little bit credible …

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Recentering African Feminist Epistemologies: A Community of Practice to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence
content:
Over the past year, Liberation Alliance Africa has sustained the

Building Knowledge Bridges Community of Practice on Recentering African Indigenous Epistemologies to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence

. This Community of Practice is a collective of African feminist scholars, practitioners, organisers, artists, and movement builders committed to the dreaming and making of a world free from sexual violence through knowledge bridges.


Sexual violence continues to impact communities across the African continent, and class, ethnicity and religion play a critical role in making civilians in conflict-affected countries particularly more vulnerable. It disproportionately affects women and girls, and ethnic, gender and racialized minorities. Sexual violence is compounded by conflict, displacement, poverty, and gender inequality. It remains significantly under-reported due to stigma and under-prosecuted? Due to weak and corrupt justice systems. Sexual violence includes rape and sexual assault, sexual coercion and exploitation, including trafficking for sexual exploitation and conflict-related sexual violence such as using rape as a weapon of war. It affects people of any gender and age. 


Our starting premise is simple: sexual violence on the continent cannot be understood, let alone addressed, through frameworks that treat colonialism as history rather than a structural force that continues to shape theory, practice, and response to sexual violence. 


Coloniality was

coined

by Peruvian philosopher and sociologist Aníbal Quijano, and it describes the long-lasting pattern of power produced by colonial rule and shape

s

 how we approach epistemological frameworks through which violence is understood.

Epistemology deals with questions concerning the nature, scope, and sources of knowledge.

 A meaningful analysis of sexual violence must begin by seeking to decolonise knowledge and epistemic structures. This analysis requires us to interrogate the assumptions that underpin dominant theories, question whose expertise is legitimised, and create space for African feminist epistemologies to shape how violence is understood, prevented, and responded to. 


We felt an urgent need to organise as scholars and practitioners to generate new frameworks grounded in our histories, political realities, and lived experiences. Our analyses are rooted in our confrontation of the neo-colonial state, the global imperialist, extractive and patriarchal systems that shape our everyday existence. We arrive as feminists in service of a liberatory project, convinced that knowledge-making is itself a site of feminist struggle. 


As the CoP came together through both intentional convening and organic growth, we began organising our work around three enquiries that we believe are critical to envisioning a decolonial feminist approach to preventing and responding to sexual violence in Africa. 


The first enquiry,

Whose Knowledge? An Audit of the Current Knowledge Systems within Sexual Violence Prevention and Response in Africa

 examines the dominant literature, asks whose voices have shaped the field, whose knowledge has been marginalised, and what becomes possible when African feminist scholarship is placed at the centre of analysis. 


The second enquiry,

 The Coloniality of Sexual Violence: Gender, Power, Sovereignty, and the Neo-Colonial State,

 advances interventions on sexual violence that explicitly interrogate the role and impact of hetero-patriarchal colonial racial-capitalism, alongside the complicity of neo-colonial states, in producing and sustaining conditions of gendered violence. 


The third enquiry,

Truth-telling and Epistemic Sovereignty in the Prevention and Response Continuum

, centres on indigenous and endogenous knowledge systems as essential practice-based frameworks for reimagining prevention, response, healing, accountability, and collective safety.


The Imperative of Recentering African Epistemologies


At Liberation Alliance Africa, we believe African women and gender-expansive people’s knowledge-making and world-building are crucial to de-westernising normative assumptions and dominant approaches. African women and gender-expansive scholars must nurture new ways of knowing and being- knowledge that doesn’t just challenge dominant views, but creates a rich foundation for how we understand reality and tackle life’s critical questions.


For a long time, African women and gender minorities were treated as …

author: Simon Ramapuputla
title: Marikana’s wounds still bleed 14 years after police massacre
content:
Fourteen years after police opened fire on striking mineworkers at Marikana, the massacre is remembered not only for the 34 men who were killed, but for their absence in the lives of their families.


For some, the memory is of a father who never came home. For others, it is the loss of a breadwinner, a brother or a son. And for those who were children when the killings happened, it is the experience of growing up with memories that have become increasingly distant, while the questions about justice remain.


At a commemoration marking 14 years since the massacre, the families, activists and academics reflected on what Marikana means more than a decade later – and on its place in South Africa’s longer history of protest, police violence and struggles for dignity.


For the Socio-Economic Rights Institute of South Africa (Seri), which has represented the families since 2012, the central question remains accountability. Seri secured payments for 35 of the 37 families whose loved ones were killed by police. Two families have received no compensation.


Seri’s executive director, Nomzamo Zondo said the compensation process itself reflected a deeper problem in how the state understood the loss suffered by the families. “Part of that is a narrative that what the state is interested in compensating is the income that the miners would have earned. They do not want to account for the husbands, brothers, sons and fathers that they took away from the families,” she said.


For Zondo, compensation alone cannot address the significance of Marikana. The state also needs to acknowledge that the massacre should never have happened, she argued: “That’s what a public holiday on the 16

th

 of August would mean. It would say: we are saying never, never again.”


She said this was particularly important given the continued use of force by police in managing protests. “We’ve seen that police continue to manage protests through the use of violence. They have continuously refused to accept that their role is to facilitate protests as a constitutional right.”


Zondo also pointed to the failure to implement recommendations made by the panel of experts on public order policing and the management of protests. The panel completed its work in 2018, but its recommendations remain largely unimplemented.


Squalid living conditions in the informal settlement, Nkaneng, in the shadow of Marikana platinum mine, a source of immense wealth for the owners in 2012, Lonmin. Archive photo by The Benchmarks Foundation


Another major concern, she said, was the failure of the National Prosecuting Authority to bring those responsible for the 16 August killings to court. “Every year, of course, when the anniversary comes, there is an explanation that work is being done,” Zondo said. “But now we are like one year short from 15 years since the massacre. We are just 12 years since the Commission finalised its report and recommended that the NPA must investigate and charge whoever is responsible.”


The question, she said, was whether there was “really an intention to hold anyone accountable for the deaths of the 16

th

 of August”.


For the families, however, the consequences of Marikana are not measured only by the progress of criminal investigations or compensation claims. They are lived in the absence of loved ones.


‘I still have that memory’


NowilI Nungu was 15 when her father, Jackson Lehopa, was killed at Marikana. Today, at 29, she remembers him through the ordinary moments of their life together: travelling to school on a bicycle, buying him a Coke and watching him repair the bicycle whenever it broke.


“I have so many memories with my dad,” Nungu said. She was the only girl among six children and had been living with her father in Rustenburg while her mother moved back to the Eastern Cape.


By the time of the massacre, Nungu had moved to the Eastern Cape with her mother. The family did not have electricity and relied on the radio for news. Her father normally called every day after returning from the koppie to tell them he was safe. But that day, he did not call.


Crosses erected at the koppie as a symbol of lives lost on 16 August 2012. Archive photo by Muzi Mzoyi


Sebolai Liau lost his father, the late Janefeke Raphael Liau, at Marikana. For him, the question of justice remains unresolved. “I think regarding the Marikana massacre, there is no justice. I don’t think it will ever be served, but for now it has not been, and there are no signs …
